recipes.name: Sunday Morning Lemon Poppy Seed Pancakes

steps.text: Stir the milk, vinegar, and lemon juice together in a bowl; let stand 10 minutes to curdle. Whisk in egg, butter, and vanilla extract.

In a separate bowl, mix together the flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, salt, poppy seeds, and lemon zest until well combined. Pour the milk mixture into the flour mixture and whisk a few times until the batter is mostly free of lumps.

Heat a skillet over medium heat and spray with cooking spray. Pour 1/4 cup of batter per pancake into the skillet and cook until bubbles appear on the surface, about 2 minutes. Flip the pancakes over with a spatula and brown the other side, about 2 more minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Sunday Morning Lemon Poppy Seed Pancakes
raw_recipe.description: The favorite flavors of lemon and poppy seed combine to make light, lovely pancakes for a special breakfast.

review.reviewBody: I made these with whole wheat flour, and 1T honey instead of sugar. Great recipe for light and fluffy pancakes!

I have made this a few times. As the recipe states it is good. To add a little more lemon flavor I use the full zest of a medium lemon as well as all the juice. I only use what is called for in the milk mixture and then add the rest of them lemon when mixing the batter. Let the batter rest a few minutes aftet mixing before cooking to allow it to fluff up a bit more. The pancakes are very good, a blueberry compote on top would put this recipe over the top.
Delicious! We are a dairy free household so used almond milk and Earth Balance “butter” and still turned out fabulous. (Did add some extra lemon juice to make it extra lemon)

Excellent recipe! I changed it only a little, I mixed a big spoonful of lemon curd into the batter. Then once I ladled the batter on to the skillet I put little tiny spoons of lemon curd and then sprinkled some frozen Maine wild blueberries on. I then drizzled on a little bit more batter just to lightly cover blueberries and lemon curd. Sinfully good sprinkled with confectionary sugar! Thanks for the recipe! :)

Not lemony enough for my liking. Sprinkle with lemon juice just before serving, and use all lemon juice instead of vinegar. Next time I'll double up on the poppy seeds. These were a great change from the normal routine. Will make again soon!

Loved this recipe. I couldn't find my poppy seeds in the freezer and it was still very good. I did made a blueberry compote to top them with and added a few drops of almond extract as someone else has mentioned in place of the vanilla in the pancake batter and also into the blueberry topping. Worth the extra steps to make from scratch!

This recipe is awesome with a couple modifications! After reading the reviews and considering I wanted to put maple syrup on these cakes and desired a more intense lemon flavor I did the following.

If you plan on serving this with a sweet blueberry sauce or maple syrup, reduce the sugar by 1/2 tablespoon. Add zest of the whole lemon to the flour mixture. Also add an additional tablespoon or tablespoon an a half (or even more) of lemon juice to the milk mixture when you're adding the butter, vanilla and egg. I will probably add even more next time. I also added an extra 1/2 teaspoon of poppy seeds.

This batter is so fluffy and light! It made three 8-inch pancakes, so while it might not serve 4 - it definitely could serve three with a side of bacon or bowl of fruit. I also plopped about 8 frozen blueberries on top of each pancake after pouring batter into my pan. Didn't weigh them down at all :) Just made them even more yummy.

This is a keeper!

These were phenomenal. Definitely added more lemon zest (about a lemon and a half) and added a little extra lemon juice in the end. I usually cook my pancakes with a lid on (adds extra fluffiness). Dust with some icing sugar and enjoy the best pancakes ever

The recipe as-is came out a little bland, so the 2nd time around, I increased the amount of lemon zest and lemon juice, plus, I added dry wheat farina (1/3 cup), honey and instead of regular milk, I used a combination of buttermilk and almond milk and instead of white sugar, I used coconut sugar. The 2nd batch with modifications were much more fluffy and quite savory. My kids and husband couldn't stop eating them, so I cooked up an additional batch for the week's breakfast. They taste delicious with fresh fruit strawberries too! All-in-all, very satisfied, and will definitely make them again!

Truly 5 star pancakes. I suggest doubling the recipe for a happy family of 4 (with leftovers) and for ease of ingredients. One full lemon zested & that same lemon juiced is perfect for the double recipe. Want to zest it up? Try adding vanilla chips or substituting some or all of the butter with coconut oil.

Delicious! Like eating cake for breakfast. We doubled the lemon zest and kept everything else per the recipe. Don't over cook them. We flipped them when they were golden with no bubbles forming yet and it was perfect.

Changes were to use melted coconut oil instead of butter, 1 teaspoon of vanilla, 1.5 cups of flour, honey instead of sugar, omitted the poppy seeds, used the zest of a whole medium lemon, and added all of the juice of that same medium lemon. I also used coconut oil on the frying pan instead of butter.
This recipe was exactly as advertised. The lemon poppyseed flavor was palpable. Decadent, fun experience and we’ve made them four times since trying it just a few weeks ago.

Made these pancakes for a small group of adults & everyone raved about the bright lemony flavor! We had to use gluten free flour & we took some reviewers suggestions to double the lemon zest & skip the vinegar… it was absolutely delicious 😋 I plan to make this again soon for the extended family at the lake.

Super easy recipe and very delicious! I've made it twice already and will continue to make more. I added extra lemon zest and vanilla. I tried it both with regular milk and almond milk as well. I made lemon curd also and had it with the pancakes - delicious!
Such a light pancake! I used 2 tablespoons of lemon juice and eliminated the vinegar. I doubled the amount of (clear) vanilla also. This yielded about 16 - 3 inch pancakes.
tasted like ants covered in flour... wouldnt make again.

These were excellent. They weren’t as thick as a traditional buttermilk and instead were light and fluffy. I don’t ever follow recipes but this one I did and it was well written. For the vinegar I used a raspberry vinegar which worked well. I paired them with a vanilla kefir lebnah.

These were amazing! Turned out very light and fluffy. Didn’t have lemon zest so used orange zest. Substituted chia seeds for the poppy seeds for the health benefits. Otherwise I made as directed. Definitely will make again.

Oh my goodness, what lovely flavor! The batter is nice and fluffy. I only got 6 1/2 pancakes from this but they were delicious! I did add 1/2 tsp lemon extract to make sure the lemon flavor came through and it did!
